stories.title: Met Police trial facial recognition tech on phones
stories.summary: Met officers can check people’s faces against a database of around one million custody images.

stories.title: Piccadilly line services to stop for 24-hour strike
stories.summary: The walkout will begin at midday but TfL warns that services will stop running before that.

stories.title: Northern line upgrades give green light to colour blind drivers
stories.summary: The Northern line becomes second Tube line accessible to drivers with colour blindness.

stories.title: Police stop and search in spotlight at youth event
stories.summary: Hundreds of young people attend a summit as part of plans to overhaul the tactic of stop and search.

stories.title: London school first in England to win global prize
stories.summary: Swiss Cottage School picked up the Community Collaboration award for its work with SEND pupils.

stories.title: London Ambulance Service sees 999 calls surge
stories.summary: LAS declares critical incident after more than 7,000 calls are made for three consecutive days.

stories.title: Teen shooting organiser found guilty of murder
stories.summary: Lathaniel Burrell, 16, was shot dead in Stockwell, south London, in March 2025.

stories.title: Mayor of London announces reshuffle of deputies
stories.summary: The changes include a newly created role of skills commissioner, to support young people into work.

stories.title: Hundreds still homeless after being evacuated from 'unsafe' flats
stories.summary: Investigations continue after the Caxton Works development was declared "at risk of sudden collapse".

stories.title: Cleverly to run as Tory London mayor candidate
stories.summary: The former home and foreign secretary has been a London Assembly member and fire authority chair.

stories.title: Liverpool Street remains busiest station in the UK
stories.summary: Liverpool Street makes history with over 100 million passengers using the station in a single year.

stories.title: TfL photocard breach exposes 265,000 customers
stories.summary: Names, addresses, dates of birth and security answers were accessed, Transport for London says.
